judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 24px globe.svg icon inside the header link 'Outros idiomas' (gtranslate). Edge names the link 'globe Outros idiomas'. The alt 'globe' matches the file name, but it also correctly describes what the icon shows: a globe. It is not a meaningless filename or placeholder, so this is not F30. The icon is redundant with the link text, so alt='' would be cleaner, and an English word on a pt-BR page is clumsy. A professional audit would note that as advisory at most, not as a 1.1.1 failure. The patch 'Mudar idioma' would make the name 'Mudar idioma Outros idiomas', which only rewords and duplicates the text.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: In the 'Cidades e Estados' quick facts, code.svg is a 40px badge or ID-card icon next to the visible label 'Código Municipal' and its value (for example 1302603). An icon that labels a data field is properly described by what it stands for, so alt='Código Municipal' serves the equivalent purpose. It repeats the adjacent text but is not wrong. The suggested 'Carteira' (wallet) misreads the icon and would make the alternative worse. The real placeholder alts in this block are on the sibling icons ('MOD_QUICK_FACTS_POPESTIMADA', 'MOD_QUICK_FACTS_AREA'), not on this one.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Card 1 of 'Nossos sites'. The img (banner-avaliacao.jpg, a clipboard with a checklist and star rating) sits in a link whose visible text is 'Pesquisa de Avaliação de Serviços Participe!'. Its alt is the placeholder 'imagem banner', and Edge computes the link name as 'imagem banner Pesquisa de Avaliação de Serviços Participe!'. 'imagem banner' is not an alternative for anything. It is the F30/F39 pattern, a placeholder like alt='image'. The visible text already names the site, so the icon should have alt='' or a real equivalent. This is a genuine 1.1.1 failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the home page of the IBGE portal. 'IBGE | Portal do IBGE | IBGE' repeats IBGE, but it names the site and says this is the portal's front page. On a site's home page, the site name is the page's topic. Inner pages have their own topic titles, for example 'Mensal | IBGE' and 'Avaliação dos Dados sobre a Biodiversidade Brasileira | IBGE', so titles tell pages apart. A professional audit would not log this under 2.4.2. Spelling out the institute's full name only rewords a title that already passes.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The card is in the 'Próximas divulgações' carousel (release calendar). It gives the date and the name of the 15/10 release. The collector's destination fetch got a 403. I loaded the target live: it is the product page 'Avaliação dos Dados sobre a Biodiversidade Brasileira' (Informações Geocientíficas Experimentais). IBGE's own monthly calendar links this same release to the same page, tagged data-produto-id='38371'. So the release is registered under that biodiversity-data product, and the card follows the section's pattern, where each release links to its product page (PMS links to the PMS page, and so on). The link text accurately names the release, and its purpose in the calendar context is clear. The patch would replace the release name with the product name, so the card would no longer say what is being released on 15/10.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The card is the last slide of the 'Próximas divulgações' carousel, whose heading link and 'Calendário Completo' button also go to /calendario/mensal.html. It goes to the IBGE monthly release calendar ('Mensal | IBGE'). I loaded that page live: it lists '16/10/2026 Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios Contínua: Trabalho de Crianças e Adolescentes de 5 a 17 anos de idade 2025', which links on to the related announcement. In a release-calendar section, a card naming a scheduled release that opens the calendar entry for that release has a determinable purpose. 2.4.4 does not require the link text to match the destination's page title. The patch 'Calendário mensal de divulgações' would remove the release name and make the card less informative.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale:
The h6 heads an indicator card:
PIBSCNTAcumulado 4 trimestres
, followed by the value 1,9% and '2º tri 2026'. The small is display:block. Edge computes the heading name as 'PIB SCNT Acumulado 4 trimestres', and the snapshot's readingText also has the spaces. The snapshot name 'PIBSCNTAcumulado 4 trimestres' dropped them. Read correctly, the heading names the indicator (GDP, quarterly national accounts, 4-quarter accumulation) whose value follows, so it meets 2.4.6. The patch only rewords it.
